text:
mike_support: customer reported severe tail latency spikes on /embeddings after yesterday's runtime tweak. small payloads (single short sentences) but P95 jumped from ~80ms to ~250-600ms. they attached a repro and logs.

tara_oncall: which region/model? any error codes or dimension mismatches in logs?

mike_support: us-west, model: open-embed-1536, route uses dynamic batching with max_batch_size=128, coalesce_window_ms=20. no explicit error codes in customer app, just long waits then success. gave us an example curl and SDK call.

alex_runtime: thanks — two hypotheses: 1) dynbatch + large max_batch_size causing big batches when a few heavy/slow shards get scheduled -> tail spikes; 2) transient KV-cache misses / variant fallback causing CPU path execution for some requests. both can multiply tail latency.

joel_sre: saw similar last month tied to mixed small/large request patterns. small requests wait for coalesce window to fill up to max_batch and then a large request causes head-of-line.

mike_support: attaching the repro snippet they sent:

```
# customer snippet (python)
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="open-embed-1536", input=[s])
# they send one short sentence per request at ~600rps
```

plus thread of logs: "batch_size=1 queued, coalesce_wait=20ms, batch_executed_size=64, exec_time_ms=420" repeated.

alex_runtime: log clue: batch_executed_size=64 but max_batch_size=128 — so batches are forming okay but exec_time=420ms for that batch. need per-request timings inside batch. can we get runtime logs with token-level exec times?

mike_support: customer pasted runtime log snippet:

```
[2026-09-12T14:21:11Z] route=embeds shard=2 batch_id=987 exec_ms=418 items=64 kv_hit=false variant=quant-int8 fallback=false
[2026-09-12T14:21:11Z] route=embeds shard=3 batch_id=988 exec_ms=35 items=4 kv_hit=true variant=fp16
[2026-09-12T14:21:12Z] route=embeds shard=2 batch_id=989 exec_ms=450 items=64 kv_hit=false variant=quant-int8 fallback=true
```

tara_oncall: interesting — shard 2 shows kv_hit=false and also a fallback=true on second entry. fallback suggests we dropped to a slower path (maybe CPU or slower kernel) for some batches. that will definitely bump tail.

alex_runtime: exactly. fallback=true indicates variant incompatibility or an OOM/quant conv miss. two likely root causes: 1) model variant selection churn (fp16 vs quant-int8) when sequence-length distribution changes or memory pressure causes kernel selector to pick slower kernels; 2) intermittent dimension mismatch from upstream client or router sending small/zero-length tensors causing runtime to reconfigure.

joel_sre: also check for the "EmbeddingDimensionMismatch" logs. if older clients send 768-dim vectors into a 1536 model route, the runtime may attempt a conversion/fallback. those conversions are expensive.

mike_support: customer found one error line: "ERROR: EmbeddingDimensionMismatch: expected 1536 got 128 for request id=abc123" — they said that was from an internal client that occasionally sent a batching-placeholder.

alex_runtime: there we go. when a mismatched-dimension request sneaks into the same shard queue, runtime must handle/convert or reject. conversion path triggers fallback and prevents efficient KV caching. that plus dynamic batching coalescing to larger sizes explains P95 explosion.

mike_support: asking for remediation steps we can apply without full infra changes.

alex_runtime: short-term mitigations:
- enable strict_dim_validation=true on the route so mismatched dims are rejected immediately (fast failure) rather than hitting fallback.
- lower max_batch_size to 32 or 16 for this customer route to reduce single-batch exec time variance.
- reduce coalesce_window_ms to 5ms for mixed-traffic endpoints (helps small, latency-sensitive requests).

tara_oncall: can also add a priority_tag on small requests so they get preemptive batching lane. e.g., client sets header X-Redwood-Priority: low|high and router keeps a small fast lane.

joel_sre: medium-term: runtime should add an early-detect filter that rejects dim-mismatch before entering batch queue and a per-shard perf-stats stream exposing kv_hit ratio + variant-churn counts. i've opened SRE ticket RT-4532 to add perf counters.

mike_support: customer asked for step-by-step to reproduce so they can validate fixes. suggested repro:
1) run two clients: one sending single-sentence requests at 400-800 rps (small)
2) a second client occasionally sends malformed/padded requests with wrong-dim (128) every ~10s
3) observe P95 on host and runtime logs for fallback=true entries

alex_runtime: confirm repro steps and added snippet to force fallback for testing:

```
# force a fallback by sending truncated tensor
payload = {"input": ["..."], "meta": {"dims": 128}}
client.http.post('/v1/embeddings', json=payload)
```

(note: don't do in prod)

tara_oncall: i'll schedule a canary with strict_dim_validation and max_batch_size=32 for the customer's route tomorrow morning. if that clears P95 we'll recommend the config.

mike_support: customer is OK with config change + repro. i'll apply and report back. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment started for route=acct-1234-embeds config: {"strict_dim_validation":true,"max_batch_size":32,"coalesce_window_ms":5} - job 7421

mike_support: update — deployed to canary, customer ran repro, P95 reduced from ~420ms to ~70-90ms. they still see rare spikes ~180ms when the malformed request hits.

alex_runtime: expected. the strict validation will make malformed requests fail fast; if customer still needs to accept mixed-dim producers we should add a thin rejection+retry shim in the SDK to convert/route appropriately rather than hitting runtime fallback.

mike_support: closing for now, will reopen if spikes persist after full rollout. saved logs and repro steps attached to the ticket.

joel_sre: noted. created follow-up action: add early-dim-check and per-batch variant metrics (RT-4532).

mike_support: thanks everyone.
